r0.why: Names, 445 Ma, first of big five in [1]; global, 49-60% genera and ~85% species in [3]; sea life and rare land spores in [19].

r1.why: Second-largest by genera behind end-Permian in [2],[4]; genera more reliable and ~100 families in [20]; all major groups and one third of brachiopod/bryozoan families in [5].

r2.why: Two pulses [8]; LOMEI-1 at Katian-Hirnantian boundary [9]; glaciation over Gondwana, greenhouse to icehouse [10]; shelf habitat loss for restricted taxa [11]; Hirnantia fauna [13].

r3.why: LOMEI-2 in later Hirnantian as ice receded [14]; worldwide anoxia and euxinia into Rhuddanian [15]; third-pulse debate [16],[17]; Hirnantia fauna replaced [43].

r4.why: Deep-water and tropical endemics [39]; Foliomena fauna lost in first pulse, habitat loss [40],[41] (which also tie the end-Katian pulse to the first pulse); inarticulates [34]; Spiriferida/Atrypida [37]; abundance [38].

r5.why: Recovery over first 5 Myr of Silurian [7]; simpler, broader-niched communities [27]; endemic to cosmopolitan faunas [29]; few long-term impacts and faster recovery than P-T [30],[31].
